title: M100, NGC 4321
caption: The spiral galaxy M100, imaged by the WIYN 0.9-meter telescope at Kitt Peak

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Strong blue spiral arms, lit by young stars, wind around the centre of M100, a nearly face-on spiral galaxy of type Sc. Two small dwarf galaxies nearby also appear in the frame, and the picture manages to show them without letting M100's bright inner regions overflow into a white glare.

M100 ranks among the brighter members of the Virgo Cluster, even though on the sky it lies within the neighbouring constellation Coma Berenices. A galaxy cluster is a large family of galaxies bound by gravity, and the Virgo Cluster is home to many of the galaxies in Messier's catalogue.
The blue colour of the arms is a sign of recent star birth. Young, hot, massive stars shine blue, and in a spiral galaxy they tend to be strung along the arms, where gas gathers and new stars form.

understand.summary: The WIYN 0.9-meter telescope at Kitt Peak captured M100 in visible light; the filters and colour mapping are not published.
understand.eye: The camera's exposures gather far more light than the eye and can hold both the bright core and the fainter arms in one frame.

explore: The WIYN 0.9-meter telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory captured this image on the night of 20 December 2002 (Universal Time), and covers 15.3 arcminutes. Other Messier galaxies in the Virgo Cluster include M49, M58, M59, M60, M61 and M84, as well as M85, M86, M87, M88 and M89, plus M90, M91, M98 and M99.
alt: A nearly face-on spiral galaxy with blue arms around a bright centre, and two small dwarf galaxies nearby.
